3-Alkenoates are a class of compounds with synthetic importance due to the uniquely located carbon- 
carbon double bonds. These compounds can be, in principle, prepared via either oxidation reactions of 
the corresponding alcohols/aldehydes or carbon-carbon double bond formation reactions. The major prob- 
lem for their synthesis is the potential migration of the C+C bond from the p, y -pition to the a, p- 
Allenes are important intermediates in organic synthesis due to the unique reactivity arising from the 
existing two orthogonal x-bond~.~'~ During the course of our study of allene chemist~y,~'~ we found that 
the hydrohalogenation reaction of unsubstituted 2,3-butadienoic acid and its methyl ester with MX in 
HOAc affoded 3-halo-3-butenoic acids and esters in high yields and selectivity.5* h this paper we wish 
to report our recent results of the hydmhalogenation reaction of substituted 1 ,2-allenyl carboxylic acid es- 
ters and the corresponding synthetic application of the p, 7-unsatutrated 3-halo-3-alkenoic acid esters thus 
formed. 
The reaction of 2-alkyl-2,3-alkadienoates with HX is synthetically uninteresting since it afforded a 
mixture of a, p-unsaturated 2-alkenoates and p, 7-unsaturated 3-alkenoates. Thus, we tried the hydm- 
halogenation reaction of ethyl 2-methyl-2,3-butadienoate with NaI in HOAC.~" However, it also yielded a 
mixture of a, p-unsaturated 3-iodo-2-methyl-2-butenoate (3a) and p, 7-unsaturated 3-iodo-2-methyl-3-
